Tommas avoids you for the rest of the day. When the lessons end, he quickly packs up and leaves without you.
You spend the evening with Diederik and his retinue. As it turns out, the children of noblemen aren’t so bad when you get to know them — they are simply afraid for their status and eager to avoid being mixed up with the lowborn boys.

Not Diederik himself, however — his stupidity and bravado are astonishing. He clearly became their leader through sheer audacity and overconfidence. However, you always remember exactly why you need his friendship.
Several days pass, and then Diederik invites you to his family’s house.
You inform Father of the invitation.
“You have made friends with the City Hall secretary’s son? This may bode well for our family. Well done! I will accompany you there.”

Both of you travel to the City Hall district when the time comes. The secretary’s house is larger and more luxuriously decorated than your family’s. There is even a garden in front of it, planted in imported soil.
Diederik pompously introduces you to his father, a balding, aloof-looking nobleman.

The two fathers sip wine until the sun goes down, discussing Anizotte affairs such as the Quorum Decree, the Lesser Quorums, the policies of Archduke Milanidas, and the new agenda set by Prefect El Borne. Father doesn’t forget to mention that he is related to the prefect.

The two fathers part on good terms — they agree to invite each other to dinners and aid each other in work-related matters.
You take the carriage back home. Father tousles your hair tipsily.

02.07.01.title: The Silver Tree

buttons.ButtonDescription1: What truth will you learn inside the temple?
buttons.ButtonDescription2: What else does she have to say?
buttons.ButtonDescription3: The Tree… it knows more than any human…
buttons.ButtonDescription4: You open yourself to the Tree and listen as it speaks.

consequences:
You turn your back on the suspicious preacher and follow the girl inside.
She introduces herself to you along the way. Her name is Jeanne.

Jeanne’s voice is clear and insistent. As you listen to her, you just barely touch the palm of your hand that held hers a moment ago.
Maybe it’s just a delusion… but that hand feels warmer now.

You keep looking back at the Tree all the way home.
But it is not the Tree you see. You see Jeanne’s brown eyes, filled with inscrutable wisdom.

The temple is filled with light. It is separated into two halves, just like the temple in your district: one for the commoners and one for the nobles. Yet this temple is far more grand than that one.
You see two towering statues by the altar, carved with impeccable detail. They depict the Twins. The Elder bears an empathetic smile, and the Younger has a stern look about him. They are depicted in the garments of pilgrims, frozen in Their eternal journey to meet one another.

“My uncle is one of the priests in this temple. I’m an acolyte. I work in the temple — I help him, clean the temple, and cook food for the poor. And I also greet the worshippers! People come here all the time! Many are lost, and they don’t know where to go once they’re inside. But nobody should feel lost in this place — the temple is for all the estates.”

Jeanne’s face is no longer angry — the red-haired preacher is long forgotten. She is like a warm ray of light under the roof of the grand, bright temple.
You ask her a question: is she happy in her service to the Twins?
“Of course I am! This is where I belong. Inside the temple, I feel the Twins watching over me all the time. When I’m with them, I’m never afraid, never sad.”
She looks at the statues when she mentions the Twins and smiles at them as if they are her close friends.
“Do you feel it too?”

You, too, turn your eyes to face the Twin Gods.
You feel the eyes of the Elder upon you. They feel warm, warm like Mother’s loving words.
You feel virtue and order in the eyes of the Younger. They feel like Father’s words of pride and respect.

“I knew it, I knew you could feel it! It’s so easy when you’re in the temple. But they watch over us all the time, you know. Just pray from your heart and remember how it feels all the time. Even back home. Even on a long, long journey!”

You shrug, smile sheepishly at the girl, and walk towards the red-haired preacher.
This Matilde of Astinia… she speaks too strangely to be ignored. You feel she will be leaving soon anyway.
And the temple… surely the temple is not going anywhere.

The lady preacher hands her book to you.
There are words on the cover: “The Lives of the Twins.” The book is so heavy, you almost drop it.
The crowd around you barely allows for a proper reading. The best you can do is flip through the pages and hope to glimpse a message or two from it. Matilde’s hushed voice comments on each new page.

This book was written by the disciples of the Twins. When the Twin Gods descended and brought faith into the world, they walked the lands with Them.
It is filled with many stories of wonders and battles, as well as records of the Twins’ own sermons and dialogs. They discuss many things that now guide the living: the fate that awaits us on the Shining Pillar, the eternal life after final death, the profane evil of magic…

Yet Matilde points out something that you cannot help but notice yourself: there is not one mention of the Lots in this book. 
”How can this be?” you ask her.
”It is what it is,” she responds. “The Twins never spoke of them. They never left any teaching behind — nothing but their deeds and their own lives in this world!”

You frown. Then how come we know about the Lots now?
”They exist thanks to Isatius,” she says. “Isatius, favored by the gods, the Elder’s favorite disciple, walked the lands by His side and through all His hardships until His fatal end in Eterna. They came to be,” she explains, “when people came to Isatius and asked him how they should live.
”Yet Isatius was but a man, and his teachings of the Lots were not a divine revelation, but a speculation of his own devising.”

This feels much tougher than learning prayers. 
So if the teachings of the Lots come not from the Gods, but rather from Their student… what does that mean for you? What does it mean for the people?
”A New Faith,” the red-haired preacher says with a smile.
You think about her words for a long time as the Silver Tree whispers above your head — the very tree grown from the blood of the people who walked the land with the Younger and the Elder.

You keep on thinking about it even as you make your way home and into bed.
Your conclusions bring you no comfort.
If that strange lady preacher was right, then you are supposed to be free to interpret the Twins’ words yourself, which means that you and only you should be responsible for your life and fate in the hereafter.
But who can tell for sure?

You cannot fall asleep that night. So they were lying to you all this time?
In the morning, you still mutter off a prayer and the words of your Lot: “to work, endure, and suffer…” but is it all worth it if the Lots don’t really exist?
Or is it the will of the Twins after all? Did They actually speak their will through Isatius, and those who defy that Will are defying the true order of the world?
These questions will remain in your mind for a long time.

The Tree is beautiful.
The silver-white foliage stretches and spreads towards the sky, held aloft by a trunk so thick it would be a challenge to walk around it. The leaves rustle and whisper peacefully in the wind.
The Tree… it seems to speak to you.

You walk away from the odd-looking preacher and the young acolyte, ignoring them as they call out to you.
You walk around the temple and the crowd of people, getting closer to the Tree with every step.
Then you extend a shaking hand and touch the bark. It is unusually warm. You can feel a pulse beneath the roots.
The Tree is alive.

The roots are so gigantic, they form large grottos, spaces of air embraced by the roots and the ground.
You squeeze into one of these grottos. It is unusually bright and quiet, shielded from the noise of Anizotte.
Right now, there is only you and the Tree.

You sit down. There are leaves rustling all around you.
The only noise you hear is the beating pulse of life that flows through the Tree.
And this pulse beats in time with your own heart.

You feel clarity and calmness, free of doubt and frustration. 
The Tree speaks to you — or are they your own thoughts, so strange and so unfamiliar and so eye-opening?
These thoughts speak of soothing Love; and of crystal-clear Law; and of Love and Law intertwining to bring the miracle of life to you.
You stop slouching, and your frown becomes a light smile.
Hours pass like fleeting seconds.

You lose track of time until you overhear someone shouting your name. 
Alas… it is time to leave this grotto.
The sun is setting over Anizotte now. The day was quick to pass.
Your teacher frowns, ready to scold you. You mumble an explanation and say you are ready to be punished for disobedience. Yet, instead, the teacher nods in understanding.

You keep looking back at the Tree all the way home.
Whatever happened to you today, you find it difficult to put it into words.

You step away from the girl in black and the woman in white, your eyes transfixed by the tremendous towering trunk of the Tree.
For some odd reason, you recall Mother’s ant farm, with the ants hard at work inside, and her face as she explained its laws. It is a fleeting, distant memory, a child’s realization about the workings of the world at large.
And at this very moment, you see yourself and all the other people for the ants they are.

You come back to your senses. You are still standing by the Tree, firmly rooted to the ground. The branches release you; and you are once again aware of the pilgrims’ prayers and the noise of the crowd.
The young girl in black is staring at you. She is clearly agitated.
“My uncle is a priest, and he told me the Twins can choose to speak with you through the Tree… but I’ve never seen it happen before!”

Jeanne starts asking you questions. She wants you to tell her what you just experienced. 
But you cannot speak. It is so difficult to see the temple’s familiar interior again, to see the district around it and the sky above. 
The memory of the sight from atop the Silver Tree now gleams in your mind.

“I just hope you’ll share your revelation with me someday. Don’t worry, I’ll get it. My name’s Jeanne. I’m an acolyte. I work in the temple — I help my uncle, clean the grounds, and cook food for the poor. And I also greet the worshippers!”
“People come here all the time! Many are lost, and they don’t know where to go once they’re inside. But nobody should feel lost in this place — the temple is for all the estates…”

But then you hear your theology teacher calling you. It is time for your class to return to the school.
Before you leave, Jeanne suddenly takes your hand. You can’t help but blush.

“Please listen to me — few people ever see these things. The Twins, they were speaking to you, and you heard them. It’s a sign! You should become a priest! 
“You’ll be guiding those who cannot hear the Twins — you’ll be helping their souls find the way to the top of the Pillar! It’s the most honorable calling in the world!”

You say goodbye to the young acolyte.
Yet as you return to your ordinary life, Jeanne’s words remain in your memory from that day forth.

You cannot look away from the Tree.
The people around you begin to fade away; their voices melt together and disappear. The world that surrounds you feels frozen and still now.
The slow swaying of the rustling branches is all there is. The branches catch you and raise you up.

You soar in the air, higher and higher along the trunk of the Silver Tree. The branches, the leaves… their light is blinding.
Their light holds you up and embraces you.

And at this moment, you realize something, something as clear as the daylight beating down on you from high above.
This Tree is divine. There is no doubt left in you: the Tree was planted by the Twin Gods and left in this land, an ever-living proof and a mark of the Twins’ existence.

And the Tree… it speaks to you; speaks in a language you understand, in the language you learned long before you were born. 
It speaks of soothing Love; and of crystal-clear Law; and of Love and Law intertwining to bring the miracle of life to you.

From this high up you can clearly see all of the land below. From here you see the entire Empire, embroidered with a shining thread of providence, illuminated by the Twins’ presence.
It takes you but a moment to finally realize what the teachers have been talking about all this time.
The fates and Lots of the people, the workings of life and the Empire… it was all created and arranged by the Twins, and absolutely everything bears Their mark, Their design and inspiration!
And it is in this world that you were given life.

Somehow, the Tree seems to realize that the revelation is now fully within you. It gently lowers you back down to the ground.
You glide down between the glowing branches, illuminated by what you have just seen.
“You… you spoke to them?”

02.07.02.title: The Shadow of the Past

buttons.ButtonDescription1: Regardless of her origins, Gloria will always be family.
buttons.ButtonDescription2: What is good for the family is good for you. You will be more wary when dealing with Gloria from now on.
buttons.ButtonDescription3: You do not want to disappoint Mother or Gloria, but you are not ready to promise anything just yet.

consequences:
Filled with determination, you assure Mother that Gloria is and will always be your sister.
You want Gloria to be a Brante too; you want her to be a part of your family. Who cares what the nobles of Anizotte say?!
Mother beams with quiet joy when she hears this.
“Oh, <username>! If only you knew how happy that would make me! To have our family united at last!”
However, the joy on her face quickly gives way to concern.

“But I already owe good Sir Robert a debt I can never repay. He’s given my daughter so much: a home, an education, his care and advice… the Brante bloodline could suffer so much from Gloria’s existence. We should all just learn to accept her status as it is.”
Just then, you hear Gloria carefully knock at the door of mother’s chambers.
“Mother! <username>! I couldn’t find you…”

You happily greet your sister. Yes, she is your sister. No old secrets can ever change that.
Mother gives you and Gloria a kiss on the forehead and returns to her prayers.

You and your sister walk downstairs together. Mother is alone by her bedside now, thanking the Twins with a quiet prayer for the Brante family They have given her.
You hope They can hear her.

You stand up straight, then softly and politely thank Mother for her warning.
From this point on, you will be more wary and prudent when it comes to Gloria. You are not a noble yet, but you are still responsible for the family’s reputation.
You understand very well that internal family matters could drag the family into dishonor at any moment.
Mother’s eyes fill with sorrow and understanding.

“That’s right, <username>. You’re right to put your family first. It is your duty to carry on the bloodline, after all.
“No matter what happens to me or Gloria, I will always be grateful to this home for everything it has given us.”
You cut her off. You and Mother are discussing something important. Gloria should wait until you are done.
“Why, <username>, you’re growing up quickly… did you learn that from your elder brother? Or Grandfather, perhaps?”

Gloria snarls back at you, but still does as she is told and leaves.
With a sigh, Mother gives you a kiss on the forehead and returns to her prayers.
When you leave, Mother remains alone by her bedside, thanking the Twins for the gift of humility with a quiet prayer.

You do not want to disappoint Mother or Gloria, but you also do not want to make any promises you cannot keep. Who knows what the future may hold?
It always pays to be careful.

And so you hide your true feelings and offer Mother a guarded response.
You are not grown up enough to have a say in matters such as these. You will not be in charge of the family’s affairs any time soon.
Of course Gloria means a lot to you, and she always will, regardless of her status in the Brante home.
Mother nods sadly.

“I understand, <username>. You want what’s best for everyone. You don’t want to betray your sister, but you also don’t want to give her too much hope. You’re still young — you don’t have to make a choice just yet. But you will have to decide one day, I’m afraid. The world won’t let you stand aside forever.”

You greet your sister as if the past few minutes never happened. You suggest reading some ancient poetry down in the library together. Gloria agrees, suspecting nothing about what Mother told you just now.
Mother remains alone by her bedside, thanking the Twins for the gift of humility with a quiet prayer.

02.08.01.title: The Nobleman’s Lot

buttons.ButtonDescription1: You grab the heaviest rock you can find and get ready to fight.
buttons.ButtonDescription2: You get busy defending Stephan while his sword does the attacking.
buttons.ButtonDescription3: You leave the fighting to Stephan and run for help.

consequences:
The louts try to flank Stephan and surround him.
Your brother’s sword thrusts and feints methodically, like in a training bout. The thugs keep dodging and jumping away. They’ve managed to stay safe so far. If things continue like this, soon one of them will flank Stephan, kick the sword out of his hand, and bring him down.
The ruffians are paying no attention to you, however.
For the first time in a long while, your brother looks at you as an equal.
“It was a pleasure to fight side by side. I’m glad you and I are brothers.”

For a moment, you want nothing more than to run away. You belong to the common Lot — you are not allowed to bear arms, not allowed to fight!
But then you take one more look at Stephan, who is almost surrounded, and at Gloria, sprawled out on the ground…
“I can’t act in any other way, can I?”
Your brother’s words ring in your ears. You cannot run. You have to help him, no matter what.
You pull a heavy rock out of the old wall.

The tow-headed leader of the gang appears behind Stephan’s back, ready to knock him down.
No time to think.
It takes you three steps to get to the foe.
No time to think!
You bash the thug in the head with the rock.
The wretch stumbles and falls down.

Stephan seizes an opportunity to strike and lunges at the louts. They scatter under his blows. You hear screams and the swishing of the sword.
You assault them too, swinging away with the heavy rock…
Until you catch something pointy in the side.

A wave of pain washes over you. Blood starts flowing down your side and onto your leg.
Stephan shouts something, but your mind is already fading fast.

When the darkness disperses, you find yourself lying in your bed. Stephan is in the armchair next to you reading a book.
He is alive! With left arm in a sling and a black eye, but still alive!
As for you, it hurts so much when you try to breathe. You cannot help but moan quietly. Stephan looks up from the book.
“Don’t try to get up. You lost a lot of blood. Fortunately, the archduke’s guards got there too late to see you swinging that boulder around. They’d have shown you no mercy otherwise.”

“But I’m impressed, <username>. You were unarmed, but you still fought them. You acted in defiance of your Lot, that much is certain, but you fought for our family’s honor. You know, brother, the nobleman’s Lot is also a great burden that few are able to bear. It takes courage — not to fight everything you see, but to do your duty! Each and every decision a nobleman makes becomes a part of his family’s legacy, flowing in the Blood Tide forever.”

“I think about it often. A noble mustn’t act weak, a noble mustn’t suffer like people of the lowborn Lot. A noble must rule over them wisely. A noble must ensure that they have work to do. It’s not merely your own Lot you have to look after — you have to ensure that a thousand others can live by their Lot as well. And there are so many more matters to take care of: honor, dignity, tradition… it’s tough, but it’s what it takes to be a nobleman. Do you understand what I’m talking about?”

Stephan’s firm voice fills you with confidence. You follow your noble brother’s orders.
It takes a moment to grab a stick, and then you are at Stephan’s back, angrily swinging at the louts as they try to bring him down.
There is approval in your brother’s eyes, for the first time in a long while.
“It was a pleasure to fight side by side, brother.”

One of the louts lunges at your brother with a stone, but you hit him with the stick, and he falls down right at Stephan’s feet.
His sword flashes. The blade sinks deep into the young man’s stomach. He wheezes. Blood starts pouring onto the ground.
The thugs freeze.
Stephan pulls the sword out, his face an inscrutable mask, and returns to his fighting stance.

You are stunned to see Stephan take another man’s life so easily and effortlessly, like picking his own teeth.
The thugs look like they are about to flee. There is rage and confusion on their faces — they never expected the young nobleman to use that sword.
Stephan just scoffs at them.
“Lowborn scum, that’s all you are! This is the only language you understand. Good job, brother. Gloria, get up — we’re going home.”

He turns to glance at your sister, giving the enraged thugs just enough time to rush you.
You get separated from Stephan; your back is against the wall now.
They hit you hard — in the stomach, then the face, then the side of the head.
Then your mind slips away.

When the darkness disperses, you find yourself lying in your bed. Stephan is in the armchair next to you reading a book.
He is alive! With left arm in a sling and a black eye, but still alive!
Your head is spinning, and you feel nauseous. You try your best to sit up. Stephan looks up from the book.
“Don’t try to get up. You lost a lot of blood. I suppose that was a few thugs too many for a single warrior, even with good backup.”

“I’m impressed. We fought like an army: the noble orders, the commoner obeys, all according to our Lots. We defended the family’s honor together. You know, brother, the nobleman’s Lot is also a great burden that few are able to bear. It takes courage — not to fight everything you see, but to do your duty! Each and every decision a nobleman makes becomes a part of his family’s legacy, flowing in the Blood Tide forever.”

Stephan slashes with his sword. One of the young men falls. The others rush at your brother.
You get Gloria back on her feet as she stares at you in astonishment. It’s time to find the guards.

You find guards dressed in the archduke’s colors patrolling the nearby district. You tell them that a gang of lowborn thugs have assaulted a young nobleman.
But when you make your way back, the louts’ bodies are already fading away. Stephan is on his feet, his sword sinking in the last foe left standing.
He smiles at you faintly, then his eyes roll back into his head, and he collapses.
The guards help you bring Stephan back home.

Grandfather sends for the doctor the moment he sees that his favorite grandson is unconscious. The doctor quickly brings Stephan back to his senses and bandages the injuries on his left arm.
Sir Gregor never leaves Stephan’s side.

“You acted like a true nobleman, Stephan. You fought for the family’s honor, even though you needn’t have risked your life for that freeloading wench. The burden of a noble is a tough one to bear: we must obey our Lot so that the lowly estate may toil for theirs. But when the lowborn scum grow insolent, we must be there to put them in their place!”

“Now I fully believe that, thanks to you, the Brante name will be written in the Blue Book, my boy! Your deeds will forever be remembered in our family’s Blood Tide. And all of us will be there: you, your father — all of us. Words cannot express how proud I am of you!”

You leave your brother’s side without a word. Grandfather will never recognize you as Stephan’s equal and Father’s true heir. He will never treat you as part of the family! He thinks you will not add a single worthy deed to the family’s Blood Tide! You, Nathan, Mother — he acts like all of you are unworthy to even bear the Brante name!
Had you acted differently that night… would Grandfather be proud of you?
Who knows?

02.09.01.title: Trial of the Assailants

buttons.ButtonDescription1: You will do as Father told you and avoid mentioning Gloria to the court.
buttons.ButtonDescription2: You agree with Father now, but you will tell the truth later.
buttons.ButtonDescription3: You are determined to change Father’s opinion and make sure Gloria gets the fair treatment she deserves.

consequences:
You nod in agreement: you will follow the family’s plan for the trial to the letter.
A faint smile appears on Father’s fatigued face.

Did you do the right thing during the trial? Your sister is still being bullied. No one knows she has a family to defend her, and Gloria does not want to be defended now.
Those four commoners saw no mercy — their lives ended for assaulting a nobleman. 
What did you seek to prove with this, and to whom? Was it worth it in the end?
“Thank you, son. This is an important case for our family, and for me as well. I appreciate your support.”

The day comes. The trial takes place in the Lesser Hall of the city prefecture. Sir El Borne himself presides as the judge.
You are seated next to Father and Stephan. You testify to the court one after another. You echo your brother’s testimony to the letter.
The young commoners insulted you as you were both walking by the ruins. Then they assaulted you. Stephan defended you.
The lives of the four thugs are forfeit.
Sir El Borne rises to deliver the sentence.
“The Court of Anizotte judges you guilty of assaulting Stephan Brante, a nobleman. All four defendants are sentenced to final death by hanging.”

There is no wind, but you feel a gust sweep through the hall. The defendants turn pale. Their mothers are bawling and crying.
Everybody in the court feels the dreadful power of the Law, and it is stern and just. That very power has been invoked by this sentence, and by that very sentence the lives of the four young men are literally forfeit — for all eternity.

The gallows await.
Stephan and Grandfather stand in the front row. The wood creaks. The trapdoors open under the young men’s feet. They dangle in the air, wheezing and reaching out for support with their feet in their final moments.
Father lets out an inaudible sigh of relief.
It is all over now.

When Gloria comes back home the day after, she refuses to eat dinner and locks herself in her room. Before she leaves, however, you notice a scratch on her face, and her hair is disheveled.
You go to her room and knock at the door, but she will not open. Then she finally replies: she has already gone to bed, and you should leave.

The carriage is silent as your family drives home. Father asks to you go to the sitting-room: you need to talk. Alone.
The tone of his voice does not bode well for you.
The sitting-room doors slam shut behind him.
“You have absolutely no idea what you’ve done! Why did you have to be so foolish and stubborn?! Why?! Explain to me!”

Father is furious.
You try to explain yourself: you only wanted them to treat your sister fairly.
Father’s face turns red, just like Grandfather’s did.

“Treated fairly, he says! His sister, he says! Get out of my sight this instant, both of you! You’re in for a world of punishment, young man — you and your sister. You are nothing but a disappointment to me. Begone!”

Next, Father gives his orders. You and Gloria are flogged together, brutally enough to ensure you learn your lesson.
Once this ordeal ends, your sister thanks you through tears — at least you tried to stand up for her. Your back will not hurt less for that, but at least you feel better now.

When Gloria comes back home the day after, there is a fresh bruise on her cheek. Her dress is covered in dust, and her hair is disheveled.
You ask her about it, but she does her best to pretend nothing is wrong. When you ask about the bruise, she says she just fell.

You meet those four commoners on the street a few days later. They thank you mockingly and tease you mercilessly. “Sir <username> Brante,” they call you sarcastically.
You walk away as fast as you can. They laugh behind your back.
Whatever happens now, Stephan will not protect you or Gloria anymore.

You watch Father leave your room and consider your options. When should you mention Gloria during your testimony?
There is no way you will pretend she was not there — that would not be fair in the slightest!

The day comes. The trial takes place in the Lesser Hall of the city prefecture. Sir El Borne himself presides as the judge.
You are seated next to Father and Stephan. You are to testify to the court one after another.
Your brother’s testimony follows Father’s plan to the letter. The young commoners insulted you as you were both walking by the ruins. Then they assaulted you. Stephan defended you.

You are next to speak.
You tell the court the truth about that night.
How the thugs humiliated Gloria; how Stephan and you came to help her; and how Stephan defended his half-sister.

There are confused whispers in the hall.
The commoners on trial cry out: it’s the truth, Gloria was reciting poetry, and they simply told her she was defying her Lot.
The situation has changed. By this account, Stephan was not acting in defense of himself or another, he merely assaulted them first in order to retaliate against those who had insulted his half-sister.

Grandfather’s face turns red, yet he remains silent.
All emotion disappears from Father’s face. 
Your brother turns to look at you, disappointed.
Sir El Borne rises to deliver the sentence. There is bitter regret in his voice as he speaks.

“With this new evidence in mind, the Court of Anizotte finds you not guilty of assaulting Stephan El Brante, a nobleman. However, you are found guilty of disgraceful conduct and injury to a noble. All four defendants are sentenced to twenty lashes each.”

You look Father straight in the eye and tell him what you think. You are not going to bear false witness in court! He is a judge himself — how can he make you lie to Sir El Borne?
And what of Gloria? Is she not a Brante too? Does she not deserve justice? Or maybe Grandfather is right, and she is just a freeloader who deserves nothing but shame? If so, then how come Father agreed to take her into his home and under his protection?

“The Court of Anizotte finds you guilty of assaulting Stephan El Brante, a nobleman, who stood in defense of the honor of Gloria, a member of his household.
“All four defendants are sentenced to final death by hanging.”

There is no wind, but you feel a gust sweep through the hall.
The defendants turn pale. Their mothers are bawling and crying.
Everybody in the court feels the dreadful power of the Law, and it is stern and just. That very power has been invoked by this sentence, and by that very sentence the lives of the four young men are literally forfeit — for all eternity.

The gallows await.
Stephan stands in the front row; father stands next to him. The wood creaks. The trapdoors open under the young men’s feet. They dangle in the air, wheezing and reaching out for support with their feet in their final moments.

Grandfather’s silence ends at home.
He screams at you and Father, at Stephan and Gloria: this trial is a disgrace! His screams are punctuated by the thudding of his walking stick against the floor.
Father says they had to defend their family. It would have truly been a disgrace if they had shirked their responsibilities.
Stephan excuses himself to bandage his arm in order to stay out of the argument.
Gloria is quiet, but glowing.
You stay quiet too. It is all over now.

It is all over now. 
Nobody bullies Gloria on the streets anymore. Those four commoners are dead forever. Their families were taught a cruel lesson - so will it be with anyone who dares to raise his hand against a nobleman.

Saying this to Father is tough. Deep inside, you pray he hears no weakness in your voice and sees no blood rushing to your cheeks.
But it seems he is listening to you intently. The wrinkles on his forehead grow deeper as his fingers stammer out a staccato against the armrest.

“This is going to be tough, son. But you’re right… you are right. I took Gloria into my home, and so I must protect her like my own daughter. This was my decision, and I must stand by it. I will speak with Stephan in the morning. Now I pray your grandfather never hears of my change of heart.”

The day comes. The trial takes place in the Lesser Hall of the city prefecture. Sir El Borne himself presides as the judge.
You are the first to testify to the court.

You tell the court the truth about that night.
How the thugs humiliated Gloria; how Stephan and you came to help her; and how Stephan defended his half-sister.
Out of the corner of your eye you watch Grandfather’s face grow red, yet he remains silent.

You spread your feet to stand firm and inhale before you speak next. You ask the hall: is it not a nobleman’s duty to honor his family name?
Gloria does not have the Brante name. But your Father took her into his home. Therefore, it was Stephan's duty to protect her - as he would have protected any of you.
Contemptuous chuckles rush through the courtroom. You have just reminded the city of Father's shameful second marriage.

Stephan is to testify next.
He reluctantly confirms your testimony, glancing at Father and Grandfather all the while.
His arm in the sling is his main argument: Stephan wanted the commoners to stop insulting Gloria, yet in the end the commoners were the first to assault him.
After a short recess, Sir El Borne returns and rises to deliver his sentence.

02.10.01.title: Agony

buttons.ButtonDescription1: You run away to wake up your siblings and rescue them from what is to come.
buttons.ButtonDescription2: You run to Mother’s side and snatch the lamp out of Grandfather’s hand before he can start a fire.
buttons.ButtonDescription3: Grandfather wishes to purge his sins. He has the right to do so, even if it costs you your lives…

consequences:
You turn around and run for your brother and sister. Grandfather’s prayers and mother’s sobbing drive you to run faster.
You wake up Nathan and Gloria and lead them out of their rooms and the house without any explanation.
You hear Mother’s shrill cry of despair from the porch.
A second floor window shatters. A body in a nightgown drops to the ground.
Then, another cry of despair — an old man’s cry.
You cover your brother’s eyes to hide the sight from him.
“You rescued your brother and sister, saved them from a lesser death… thank you, my son. Please remember this: none of this is your fault. This is my final life, and I promise to live it in joy.”
You hear the snorting of horses outside — Father is back from Eterna.

The second floor of the estate has caught fire.
Gloria runs for the neighbors. You take Nathan’s hand and go to Tommas’s house.

Neighbors and servants flock to the house to put out the fire. Together you manage to extinguish the flames before the first floor is engulfed.
The second floor, however, has been reduced to ash. You watch Mother’s body turn to dust and fly away with the sparks.
Nathan is crying. Gloria hugs him and says that everything is fine — Mother will return soon, reborn.
Tommas’s family gives you refuge for the night.

His charred body is taken to the family crypt in the morning. Gregor Brante has died his true death.
You go there to look at him.
His face is covered by the cloth, hiding its expression. Did Gregor Brante finally find solace at the Pillar amongst the flames, in his final living moments? Or did he die as he lived, an embittered soul driven mad because he could never truly live by his Lot?
Either way, life has changed. His burden no longer weighs heavy upon your family.

For a moment, you are overcome with rage. Hot tears start rolling down your cheeks. This is it — you will never be able to prove anything to him now. All your future triumphs, all your words of defiance — Grandfather will never hear them, he will never see you grow up.

You hear a heavy door clang in the corner of the crypt.
Out comes Mother, wrapped in a black cape. She is reborn.
She looks around in surprise as she leaves the cold stone walls behind, then finally notices you.
“My son… Nathan? Gloria? What happened to them?”

You briskly wipe your face and comfort her: no one else died that night. It is hard to speak — like something is clutching at your throat.
When Mother sees Grandfather’s charred remains, she closes her eyes with a deep sigh, then shakes so violently she falls to her knees.
Then she starts whispering something. You recognize it — it is a prayer of gratitude to the Twins.

When she is done, she briskly wipes her face like you did.
She looks younger now. Her eyes sparkle. She smiles, so brightly and so sincerely — you have not seen her like this for a long, long time.
Mother comes closer and pats you on the head, fondly and gently.

You look at Grandfather defiantly and step towards him. 
He stares you down with rage and throws the oil lamp at the floor.
You manage to catch it, but just barely. Several drops of hot oil hit the rug — not nearly enough to start a fire.
The lamp’s glass is blistering hot. It burns your hands, but you still hold onto it safely.
“You lowborn scum! You ruined everything — you’re every bit like your mother, you, you, you…”

Enraged, he takes a swing, and you squeeze your eyes shut.
But he does not hit you; instead, there is a deep exhalation. You peek at him with one eye — just in time to see him collapse, all his strength fading away. His chest is heaving, his face a grimace of contempt.
Another heavy exhalation. The contempt is gone. There is only fear now.
Grandfather’s eyes open wide, almost in surprise. He exhales.
His eyes grow dim.

Mother is there, whispering a prayer. She is shaking violently.
You put the oil lamp gently on the bedside table and call for the servants. They carry the body away. It does not disappear: true death has found him.
He will never return.
You spend the rest of the night with Mother in the sitting-room. She will not let go of your hand.
For many, many nights afterward she keeps seeing Grandfather’s shadow out of the corner of her eye.

Father returns from Eterna the morning after. He is unusually composed as he arranges for the funeral.
The house becomes quiet — not the looming, heavy sort of quiet of the past few months, but the calm relief you all feel now that the crazed old man is no more.
At last, Gregor Brante, the family’s patriarch, has departed for the hereafter.

You drop your hands as the grief in Grandfather’s eyes pierces your heart.
He is staring true death in the face. Those who grow old do not return from the hereafter. What fate awaits him there?
The nobleman’s Lot is to rule, but his helpless inability to fulfil his Lot — within his own family no less — is causing him so much suffering!

The servants come in time to put out the fire, but the second floor has already been reduced to ash. It will be a while before the floor is restored.
Tommas’s family gives you refuge for the night.

No matter what happened, life goes on. The family estate was damaged by the fire, yet the family continues to live there.
Grandfather’s charred body is taken to the family crypt. Gregor Brante has died his true death.
You go there to look at him.

His face is covered by cloth, hiding its expression.
Did Gregor Brante finally find solace at the Pillar amongst the flames, in his final living moments? Or did he die as he lived, an embittered soul driven mad because he could never truly live by his Lot?

You look at Grandfather’s face lit by the lamp, distorted by unyielding wrath. His force of will astounds you — even if he is using this will to choose his own demise.
To submit to this will is your duty. It is the duty of every single person in this house.
You cannot deny him.

The lamp smashes against the floor.
The carpets, the curtains, the walls — it takes a moment for the flames to engulf the entire room.

Grandfather’s hands go up as he intones a loud prayer to the Twins. You have known these words all your life, but never have they sounded so solemn.
His eyes look away, high above, his face a still mask reflected in the flickering flames.
He smiles.

You take Mother’s hands. She is crying and shaking violently, yet she will not run.
She knows it too — it is her duty to stay here.
There is only one thing you can do for her, and so you recite a prayer to her, as loud as you can, again and again and again until the acrid smoke finally fills your lungs and takes your breath away.
Gloria and Nathan are fast asleep, so they will perish before the fire seizes them… this is your final thought before a lesser death claims you.

The first thing you see in the gloom of the family crypt is Mother’s sorrowful eyes.
This is your fault. But what could you have done?
Without a sound, you mouth to her the very words she taught you: we must accept all suffering. This is the commoner’s Lot!
And even at these very moments you live by your Lot, as you lay on the cold rock of the crypt and do not turn away from Mother’s weary face.
“This is my last life.”

In the depths of the crypt you find Nathan and Gloria, reborn for the first time. 
They are shaking and crying silently — they have experienced their first death.

Mother takes the children by the hand. You leave the crypt without a word and walk to what is left of the Brante estate.
You belong to the common Lot, and so you must endure the lash of fate as it strikes again and again.

02.10.02_Funeral_Ded.title: Last Respects

buttons.ButtonDescription1: You refuse to participate in the ritual — after all, you do not bear the nobleman’s Lot.
buttons.ButtonDescription2: You still recall your first Sacrament and how you defied the Lash. You are Gregor Brante’s grandson — and so you deserve to enter his Blood Tide.
buttons.ButtonDescription3: Before you dare enter his Blood Tide, you ask Grandfather’s spirit for his blessing.

consequences:
You return the dagger to Father and say you cannot participate in the ritual. 
You are a commoner, and your back bears the mark of the Lash — Grandfather would never have let you honor his name as a nobleman.
Nathan nods in agreement — you do not deserve this honor.
Father furrows his brow and shakes his head.

“Stephan, help me close the lid of the sarcophagus. And remember to ask for Grandfather for his blessing.
“And as for you two… it seems you weren’t ready to walk the nobleman’s path after all. You’re right, son — your grandfather would never have allowed it.”

The lid of the sarcophagus falls into place with a heavy, resonant thud. 
Then, suddenly, you all freeze as each of you hears your late grandfather speak to you. His voice is loud as it rings in the depths of the crypt, and yet he speaks to each of you separately.

“Foulblood weakling! I knew you never had it in you to rise above your meager birth, <username>… you have not a drop of nobility in you, and your pathetic little brother is the same. You are a taint upon my flesh and blood — begone from my crypt!”

Your legs carry out of the crypt of their own accord. 
Out, out, out of that stuffy crypt! You can finally breathe again! 
You hear slow footsteps behind you. You turn around and meet Nathan’s gaze.

“You… you did the right thing. If it weren’t for you, I’d have done what father told us.
“Grandfather said I should stay away from his legacy — said it’ll do me no good if I try to follow in his footsteps. How’s that for words of guidance, eh?”
Nathan sighs as he embraces you.

Father and Stephan leave the crypt much later and walk to the carriage without a word. 
You and Nathan humbly follow behind them.

You remember that fateful day when you were eight, the day when you tried to choose a different Lot for yourself. You violated the ritual in the temple, you kissed the sword, and, against all odds, you said you had the right to be a nobleman.
And now you must confirm this right. You must join the Brante Blood Tide.

Cool, fresh wind blows in your face as you return to the surface. 
Stephan storms off to the carriage, fuming. 
Father stops halfway to the carriage and hugs Nathan and you briefly. Now your blood belongs to the dynasty of Sir Gregor Brante as well.

You grasp the dagger firmly, then hold the blade to your skin and quickly drag it across your palm. Drops of your blood fall into the duct, flowing further into the crypt as they combine with the blood of your father and brother.
The fresh wound burns on your hand.
“What are you doing, <username>? Why did you have to take these two along, Father? This ritual is for nobles, and you two aren’t even noblemen…”

His eyes meet Father’s stern gaze — no one is to interrupt the sacrament! 
Indignant as he is, Stephan falls silent. 
You hand the dagger to Nathan.

Your younger brother hesitates. 
Father offers him help, but Nathan shakes his head. Finally he makes a cut; and Nathan’s blood joins yours in the duct of the crypt.

The deed is done. It is time to close the sarcophagus. The lid falls into place with a heavy, resonant thud. 
Then, suddenly, you all freeze as each of you hears your late grandfather speak to you. His voice is loud as it rings in the depths of the crypt, and yet he speaks to each of you separately.

“So you think yourself my descendant, son of a lowborn woman? Very well — time will tell how much nobility you have within. But know this! I am your ancestor; you are my flesh and blood. I will be watching you always, and my shadow will follow you forever. Do not let me down, boy!”

Grandfather’s voice falls silent. 
You glance at your father and brothers, astonished. Save for Stephan, everyone else is dumbfounded as well.

The ritual is complete.
Stephan reverently kisses the grip of grandfather’s sword and places it in the alcove above the sarcophagus.
Once all is done, you leave the crypt together.

You grasp the dagger firmly, then quickly drag the blade across your palm. The fresh wound burns on your hand.
Yet before you allow your blood to join the blood of your father and elder brother, you ask your late grandfather aloud:
Will he give you his blessing to become a part of him? Will he allow you to join the Brante Blood Tide?

You hear Stephan’s indignant sigh. He does not say a word, however. 
Your words are a token of respect for Grandfather and his will. Should you obtain his blessing, Stephan will not defy the late Brante patriarch.

Then, suddenly, you all freeze.
Each of you hears your late grandfather speak to you. His voice is loud as it rings in the depths of the crypt, and yet he speaks to each of you separately.

“You had the courage to ask me for my blessing… well, so be it — you deserve an answer!
“To me, you are not incorrigible. You are half lowborn, yet you may make a worthy nobleman one day. I shall allow you to join my Blood Tide.
“But know this! I will be watching you always; and my shadow will follow you forever.
“Do not let me down, boy!”

You have Grandfather’s blessing.
You hold your hand above the opening in the wall. Your blood drips into the duct and flows further into the crypt as it combines with the blood of your father and brother.

Nathan’s turn comes. Your younger brother hesitates. 
Father offers him help, but Nathan shakes his head. Finally he makes a cut, and Nathan’s blood mixes with yours in the duct of the crypt.

Cool, fresh wind blows in your face as you return to the surface. 
Father stops halfway to the carriage and hugs Nathan and you briefly. Now your blood belongs to the dynasty of Sir Gregor Brante as well.

02.11.01.title: The Fugitive Girl

buttons.ButtonDescription1: You will protect your friend, even if you have to defy the young Arknian.
buttons.ButtonDescription2: The Arknian is within his rights. You will render him a service if you help him capture her.
buttons.ButtonDescription3: You lead the fugitive girl through the old cellar and away from the house.

consequences:
You pull yourself together and walk slowly to the half-collapsed doorway. Sophia stays behind.
The tall young Arknian stares you down, his condescending smile dripping with scorn.
In your most assertive voice, you answer his question: he will find no fugitive girl in this house.
Magic? Sophia is a witch!?

Sophia’s silhouette disappears down an alleyway. Otton’s men give her chase, but they will never find her in the dark, sprawling district.
You watch her go. Will you ever see her again?

The runaway girl becomes the talk of your district for an entire week. You overhear that Sophia managed to flee the city. The Ottons are furious.
After this sudden appearance, she disappears from your life once more. You will not see her again until much, much later.
“What are you doing here, boy? I wasn’t speaking to you. Out of my way.”

Otton needs no permission to enter, so he steps inside. 
You stand in his way. You have already assured the young Arknian there is no one else inside. You have done him a great service. What makes him doubt your words?
“Why, you lowlife! How dare you stand in an Arknian’s way! You must have lives to spare!”

Otton backhands you with immense strength, enough to send you flying. The Arknian draws his sword. It rises into the air…
But then one of his men shouts: “Sir! There she is!”
The Arknian turns around and briskly walks away.

Sophia used your distraction to climb out the window in the back!
You jump to your feet and escape the house in the same way. 
Sophia’s slight silhouette is gaining distance far ahead. One of Otton’s men is chasing her down, ready to catch her at any moment.

But then, something unbelievable happens. 
Sophia lets out a dreadful scream, and the air around her sizzles with golden sparks.
Otton’s man falls to the ground, clutching his head. Sophia freezes for a second, as though uncertain of what she just did.
What was that?
Otton screams at her right next to you.
“So that’s how it is, eh?! The wench is a witch! Seize her!”

You pull yourself together and walk slowly to the half-collapsed doorway. Sophia stays behind.
The tall young Arknian stares you down, his condescending smile dripping with scorn.
Your hand raises to point at Sophia’s hiding place.

Otton nods, satisfied. Then he steps inside, his fingers on the hilt of his sword. 
You follow him in tow.

A silhouette runs in front of you. Sophia? You hear a high-pitched scream of rage.
A golden light blinds you — a flash so bright it rends you from the inside. There is another voice in your head now, booming, screaming: “Halt! Freeze! Drop!”
You lose control of your body, your arms and legs. You collapse at the Arknian’s feet.
Sophia uses this moment of confusion to run past the nobleman and out through the door.
Otton steps over you, cursing, and runs after her.

You hear noises from the other side of the wall: running, screaming, and orders to give chase. 
You lie there on a pile of old bricks, completely unable to move.
Slowly the stupor leaves you. Finally your knees can bend again. You get to your feet, swaying, and walk out of the abandoned house.
The young Arknian is standing in the doorway, shaking his head in frustration.

“So she’s a witch, is she? Well, I’ll be… what a fascinating lass! I knew I chose her for a reason… ah, there you are, youngster. So how did you like your first brush with magic? Tell me your name. And worry not — you have my thanks.”
You tremble as you introduce yourself to Dorius Otton.
“You will go far, young Brante. You know your loyalties.”

You walk back home, lost in thought.
Sophia is a witch?! You recall how it felt, how her magic bound you by the arms and legs, how it took away all control over your body, how it made you lose the will to move. 
But that spell… you could sense something personal in the way it struck you.
Was it hatred?

You grab Sophia’s hand as you run down the stairs to the old cellar. She resists you at first until she reads your lips: there is a secret way out!
You sneak away into the cellar, leading the way. 
The floorboards groan above your heads as the Arknian and his men search the house. But only children who grew up in this district know that this cellar leads to the neighboring district.

You lead Sophia to the hole in the cellar floor and help her squeeze in. There it is: an odd tunnel that leads to a well two streets away. None of the children know who dug it, yet you played here and chased each other through it so many times as a lad.
And now, this secret passage will rescue Sophia from genuine pursuit.

Soon you are in the well. There is nothing above you save for the sky full of clouds.
You wait until you hear no more steps around you, then climb out of the well and help Sophia up.
You lead the way to the slums around the temple district — the easiest place to disappear.

A dog in a nearby house starts barking. One of Otton’s men appears in front of you. 
You take a step back as your fingers search for a brick, ready to defend Sophia no matter the cost.
She squeezes your hand, and then you hear a high-pitched scream of rage.
A flash of yellow light stuns you. In the blink of an eye, Otton’s man freezes and collapses, unable to get up.

Sophia’s eyes are no longer sky-blue — they are yellow now.
She lets go of your hand. You recoil in fear.
“You weren’t supposed to see that, <username>. Don’t worry, I won’t hurt you. But I won’t let them take me. I won’t go back to Otton after this. I need to run — run as far as my legs can take me.”
“Thank you for helping me… and farewell.”

Sophia gives you a gentle kiss on the cheek and disappears down the dark alleyway.
You stand there, stunned.
Sophia is a witch?! Her magic bound Otton’s man by the arms and legs; it made him unable to move!
You hear Otton’s screams of rage and the thumping of his men’s feet — but Sophia is long gone.
It’s a shame that was all you could do for her.

02.12.01.title: The Last Night

buttons.ButtonDescription1: You decide to peak into Father’s study.
buttons.ButtonDescription2: You go to Mother’s chambers and knock at the door.
buttons.ButtonDescription3: You think your sister is still awake.
buttons.ButtonDescription4: Surely your brother is awake at this hour… or isn’t he?

consequences:
You find Father in his study reading a book. He has been like this for as long as you can remember: always at his massive desk, surrounded by books and papers and letters, reading or writing.
You enter the study. Father looks up from his book and gives you an inquisitive glance.

After he mentions dancing, he starts speaking of something he has never mentioned to you before: Stephan’s late mother and his first wife, Amalia El Borne.
You listen to his every word, surprised by this show of trust.

“Oh, Amalia El Borne was the noble bird of prey of Anizotte, and the ballrooms were her hunting ground. Everyone thought they could tame her.
“Your grandfather saw her just once, and then he was off to Baron El Borne to negotiate the marriage. I was impressed by her, and I was so proud of myself… and yet…”

“I expected Amalia to be reborn after childbirth. But it did not happen. And when I recall it now after so many years, I see that the gods arranged it this way. Otherwise I would have never started a family with your mother.
“Oh, how much I had to suffer for marrying Lydia! But she alone is the true heart of our family…”

The sun is about to rise. You should rest before the long trip. 
Before he leaves for his bedroom, Father embraces you tightly.
“I’m so proud you’re an adult now, son. You are capable of achieving so much. Always remember that.”

You get into bed, your head spinning slightly.
This midnight talk with Father — was it about your future, or his past? Regardless, it will remain in your memory for years to come.

You want to spend the night with him before you leave. Maybe he can tell you some stories about Eterna and his own studies, or give you some fatherly advice…
Father smirks at that, as though he is plotting something.
“Have a seat, son.”
He reaches into a drawer and produces a decanter filled with rich golden liquid.
“Barley whisky — a nobleman’s drink. I think it would be good for you to try it.”

Father pulls out two glasses and pours a little of the liquid into each of them.
You take your glass and bring it to your mouth. The whisky stings your lips and palate. Father clearly savors the drink.

Father tells you a long story about his studies at the Imperial College. He had to study among the sons of the richest nobles from all corners of the land. He was but a commoner back then, and he had his fair share of hardships.
When you ask him about living in the capital, he says it was “difficult, dangerous, and full of temptation.”

“You will have your share of time in high society as well. I hope the company of nobles won’t lead you astray, son. You didn’t go to a boarding school like your elder brother, but I believe a good education and a good family still stand for something. Now, what else can I tell you before you leave?”

Father recalls the balls held in the capital when he was a youth. He even stands up from the desk and shows you a couple of moves.
Their dancing was incredibly modest: all bows and sidesteps, no touching between the dance partners.
But then again, he chuckles, those were the days when a fair lady could steal your heart with a single glance!
You nod. If anything, you know that feeling by now.

You open the door to Mother’s room. She is kneeling in prayer. Her back is to the door, and her whispers fill the room. She turns around and smiles gently when she hears your footsteps.
You want to spend tonight with her before you leave. 
Mother reaches out to you.
“Come with me, <username> — there is no need for anybody else to hear us.”
You walk silently downstairs, enter the empty sitting-room, and light the candles.
“You are so close to the gods, my son. I knew it as soon as you were born — I saw Them watching over you closely. Let us pray together, my son — may the Twins know you honor Their every touch.”

You stand by Mother’s side as she whispers prayer after prayer. First, she offers gratitude for the life and Lot you have been granted; then, a plea to show you your path through the world, for it has no mercy; next, a promise to heed and obey Their every call.
There is such fervor in her prayer, such piety! You know for certain as you pray with her that the gods will provide for you. They will ensure that your path is true.
For there is no other way.

The sun is about to rise. You should rest before the long trip, but you are not tired at all. On the contrary, you feel lucid and clear-headed.
Mother embraces you once the prayers are done.
“My son… life is hard, but it is just, moreso for those who follow their Lot. Remember: be humble in your words, and work hard.”

But before you go, Mother removes a pendant with the Twins’ cross and puts it around your neck.
You return to your room and get into bed. You can see the Shining Pillar from the window, glowing gently against the twilight morning sky. 
All your worries about the long journey are no more. You feel calm and serene.
Indeed, your sister is still awake. She jumps out of her armchair happily the moment she sees you.

Her words spark a dispute. You keep debating into the small hours.
Soon you both start reaching into history and politics and morals for material, pulling out library books one by one to prove your points. It turns out Gloria is an excellent debater — all the days and nights she spent in the library have honed her mind and rhetorical skills.
The sun is about to rise. You should rest before the long trip, but you are not tired at all.
But before you return to your rooms, Gloria locks you in a heartfelt hug.
“<username>, please promise me you’ll find your own way out there!”

You nod to her and hug her back — and then she is off.
You get into bed, but you cannot sleep.
Gloria’s words keep you up all night.
“I’m so happy you’re actually here, brother! You know, before you leave, I actually have something to tell you…”
Gloria takes your hand and leads you to the library. You light a lamp. Gloria pulls out a hefty volume from one of the shelves.

“Look! This is a history of the noble houses. It’s got the story of how humans were first ennobled.
“I read all of it, and guess what: it didn’t happen until after the expansion of the Empire. Apparently there weren’t enough Arknians for all the land — they just couldn’t rule it all by themselves!”

“Arknians have always treat humans like cattle, but human nobles are even worse. They’re like their paltry copies now! Bearing noble titles, wearing gem-studded jackets, bossing others around and poisoning their lives! They make me sick!”
“Everybody says nobles were born to rule, but if you ask me, I say they’re nobodies. There’s nothing noble about demeaning others and living off their hard work!”

Gloria is growing unusually agitated. You knew she was not exactly fond of nobles, but this is the first time you have heard such burning scorn in her voice.
But then Gloria stops herself suddenly and calms down.
“I just wanted to tell you, brother… you don’t actually have to become a noble. If you’re a noble, you’ll have to follow their rules, like Stephan does. You’re not like him. I know it.”

“Don’t listen to Mother, and definitely don’t listen to your father. They just want you to blindly follow them. It’s true, Sir Brante spent plenty of money and effort on your education… but a noble title and a judge’s rank were his dream for you, not yours. It’s time to think for yourself!”

Nathan is already in bed, snoring. You approach your brother quietly and pat him on the head.
He is startled, but starts smiling with joy when he realizes it is you.

“You’ll be leaving soon, and I’ll be all alone here. You’ll write to me, I know you will. And you’ll come back one day. But I’m scared… scared I might lose my way when you’re not around. You’ll come back, but it’ll be… different. You’ll be different. I’ll be different too.”

You swear to Nathan that even if everything changes, you will always be his brother. You will always be there to offer him advice and support. And you have no doubt that he will find his way in life.
It just takes time to find yourself — sometimes more than you might expect.

The sun is about to rise. You should rest before the long trip, but you are not tired at all. Nevertheless, it is time for bed.
Before you leave, Nathan hugs you again.
“Please promise you’ll come back, <username>.”

You swear to him that you will.
You get into bed and fade away into a gentle, happy sleep. 
They will be waiting for you back here, no matter what.
“Hi! Hey, can we go outside? I need your help with something.”

You creep silently downstairs.
The air outside is damp, and drops of dew glisten in the night. Nathan drags you towards the bushes.
A spotted kitten looks at you from the bushes with sad eyes. You see a bowl of water and some scraps of food next to it.
“Look! He ran into our yard today. See, he’s got a broken paw… we need to save the poor kitten!”

You pat Nathan on the head. Together you sneak the poor animal into the house and take him to the storage closet. Then you close the closet door and begin the treatment.
If anyone is clumsy in your family, it is Nathan, yet his hands are unusually accurate and calm as he binds the kitten’s paw.

You start chatting as you treat the kitten.
As you think out loud about living in the capital and working towards your goal, Nathan strokes the poor animal’s wet fur.
He sighs.
“It’s tough for me… you know, thinking about being a grownup. I’m not much of anything even now. I wish I could be like you! You sure know where you’re going and who you’re going to be.”
You shrug.

“No, I mean it! I can’t be like that. They say I’m going to study too, and go to Eterna and become a priest or go to the College… but there’s no way I can make it there. Does that mean there’s nothing else out there for me?”

02.N.01.title: An Adult Question

buttons.ButtonDescription1: The Twins are love for all that exists.
buttons.ButtonDescription2: Your brother is right: the Twins are stern and ruthless.

consequences:
You tell your brother that the Twins are more than just Law and Will — they are also Love. So writes Isatius, the disciple of the Elder, and so says Mother.
And both you and him were brought into this world through Their providence.

It is true that Their Love is quite unlike the love humans have for one another. They cannot forgive others unconditionally, like Mother or Father would. Your parents love you no matter what, but They are unlike them.
And yet the Twins bear no hatred, for they descended to our world and granted us knowledge of how to live. 
And this is a great treasure indeed.

The Twins put us all to the test with the hardships they send. They watch how we follow our Lots.
And if Nathan suffers and feels no love from Them, then that means They believe in him and know he will endure this suffering. They know he will humbly accept it and let it pass through him — let it purify him.
This is the manifestation of Their love.

Nathan hangs on your every word. 
The despair fades from his face — he is smiling. He puts the chain with the encircled cross back around his neck again and hugs you gratefully.
“So They do love me… thank you! You… you’ve helped me hold on to my faith.”

You hug Nathan back and hear him sniffle on your shoulder. 
He will remember this little talk for years to come.

You are quiet for a moment: and then you speak.
The Twins are stern indeed. They pay no heed to the wishes of men, for They are gods. They have Their own vision, and They follow it to guide all people to greatness.
But how can the Twins guide people when they are not people themselves?

But there is a positive side to this: you do not have to love Them either. After all, how can you force yourself to love forces that hate you just for being born? 
How can you force yourself to love entities that see you as wicked beings that can do nothing but blindly obey Their Will?

For our gods have no mercy indeed, and their law is inhuman. We have to accept it, for it cannot be changed.
But when your true death comes, there are two paths open to you: you can be brought to the Peak of the Shining Pillar, or you can be cast down into eternal suffering at the Foot of the Pillar. If you wish for the Twins’ solace and eternal bliss in the hereafter, submitting to Their Will is the only way.

Nathan hangs on your every word. 
The despair on his face is replaced by rage. He leaps to his feet. 
His fingers ball into fists. A single tear rolls down his reddened cheek.
“No! That cannot be, it is impossible, you simply cannot be right! The Twins are testing me — and they’re testing me right now too! I’m… I’m gonna tell Mom you’re spreading heresy!”

Nathan screams these words in your face and runs away, his pendant clenched in his fist instead of around his neck. 
You turn back to the book with a heavy heart. It always hurts to face the cruelty of this world. Will your younger brother weather the storm?
You know his threat means nothing. He will never tell on you.
His doubt is too great.

02.N.02.title: Forbidden Love

buttons.ButtonDescription1: If Stephan keeps acting like this, he will bring disgrace upon the entire family.
buttons.ButtonDescription2: You promise you will keep brother’s secret.

consequences:
You fold your arms as you face your elder brother.
He is confused to see you here.
You speak to him openly: you know of his affair with Maria El Velasco — and Stephan should forget that young lady as soon as humanly possible.

He freezes at these words.
You keep talking. A noble cannot behave like this. Stephan is risking bringing shame on all the Brantes — and worse yet, he is defying his own Lot and his own words. His honor, Maria’s honor, the families’ honor — it will all be harmed by his recklessness.
How could Stephan have forgotten about this? How could he have let his emotions rule him? Why should you have to be there to remind a born noble about this — you, who were born a commoner?

Stephan frowns, but lets you keep talking. You wait for his anger, but there is none.
When you are finally done speaking, your brother stays quiet for a long moment, and then sighs heavily.

“Yes… yes, indeed, you’re right. I lost control of myself. Maria— I am a madman in her presence. I forget the world when I’m with her. And I forgot my duty to my Lot and my family… I will part ways with Lady El Velasco and offer my apologies to her father. My brother… thank you. You’ve reminded me of who I am.”

From that day on, Stephan stops going out at night.
His attitude towards you has changed too. He now looks at you with respect, as if he has finally come to see you as an equal. Even in his anger, he is now quick to recall your brave decision and stop himself.
“What are you doing here at this late hour, <username>? Is there something you wish to tell me?”

You confess to Stephan that you saw him today in the El Velasco garden with the count’s daughter.
This affair puts both families’ honor at risk — yet you say you are happy for him. You can see how much he cares for her. No matter what, it is worth the risk.
Stephan can trust you with this secret, you assure him. The two of you will keep it together.
Stephan reacts to you with anger at first; but your supportive words calm him down.
“You’ve got all the makings of a professional spy! But you’re right — the risk is too great. Your aid will not go amiss — you are no nobleman yet, but I hope your word is worth my trust.”

From that day on, you help Stephan and Maria avoid attention on many occasions. You even have to distract El Velasco’s manservants and lead them away on a wild goose chase through the district. 
In the end, you are never caught, and you earn your brother yet another night with his beloved. They are both aware that the days of their hidden love are numbered.

But how will your escapades affect the family’s reputation?
You and your brother agree: whatever happens, happens. Young love is worth this risk.

02.N.03.title: The Poets

buttons.ButtonDescription1: If anyone ever hears about this poets’ gathering, it could be bad for Gloria.
buttons.ButtonDescription2: You promise to keep your sister’s secret safe and help her.

consequences:
Gloria does not leave the table. After a few moments of silence, you begin to speak.
Only nobles are allowed to create works of beauty and joy. Writing poetry is against Gloria’s Lot in life, and doubly so for poetry that mocks a noble.
This secret passion may end badly for Gloria. At best, she will get flogged; at worst, they will cut off her right hand, making her unable to write until a lesser death causes her to be reborn.

She listens to you with her eyes downcast, looking unlike the older sister you know. You keep talking.
Going to these meetings with her lowborn friends will damage the family’s reputation, and Father could even refuse to protect Gloria, especially if he realizes what her poems are about.
Finally, Gloria looks up at you. Her eyes burn with stubborn rage.
“You don’t understand, <username>! Me and my friends… without our poetry, we don’t have anything else. Nothing but our abysmal daily lives. At least we can laugh about it this way!”

Still, you insist that Gloria cut all ties with her poetry clique.
If she gets caught, all the Brantes will pay. If she doesn’t care about herself, at least she ought to think about the family that took her in!

Gloria twists her lips into a grimace and says you should leave. 
You hear no definitive answer from her.

You keep an eye on Gloria for the next few days. She no longer leaves home for long.
Has she stopped attending the secret poetry gatherings, or has she learned to hide her tracks? You never know for sure.

Gloria finally looks at you. You wink at your sister and promise to keep her secret.
You praise the poetry you were able to overhear and confess that you were impressed.
A big, joyous smile appears on her face.

“I’m so happy, brother! I thought you were about to tell me to stop going there and say what mother says about my Lot… but I’m glad you’re not like that! Me and my friends… without our poetry, we don’t have anything else left. Nothing but our abysmal daily lives. At least we can laugh about it this way.”

You get serious and tell her that her friends need to work much harder to hide their meetings. After all, this secret passion could end badly for them if they get caught. The best way out of this is to meet in a new place every time. You list off several abandoned places nearby where nobody will look for them.
You promise her that if she ever comes close to danger, you will be there to protect her.
Gloria nods and plants a kiss of sisterly joy on your cheek.

030.010.010_CulturalShock.title: Arrival in the Capital

buttons.ButtonDescription1: You forge a bond with a group of young nobles.
buttons.ButtonDescription2: You decide to listen to the speech on the rights of commoners.
buttons.ButtonDescription3: You follow the other worshippers to the temple and attend the nightly service.
buttons.ButtonDescription4: You run after the gaggle of students and join in their merriment.

consequences:
You approach the young nobles and introduce yourself tactfully. Your father, a judge, has sent you here to study, you explain.
Would they mind showing you around the capital?
The nobles eye you uncertainly and whisper to each other. You prepare to face their rejection, but, to your surprise, they agree.

The Monrogue dynasty is an ancient and controversial name. The Monrogues often speak in favor of removing humans from nobility, restoring nobility as a solely Arknian privilege, and returning all human-manned offices in the Empire to the Arknians.
Many gossipers accuse the Monrogues of plotting against the rule of the Tempests to bring back the old Arknian Republic and the joint rule of the great Arknian dynasties as it existed long before the Emperors first came to be.

The discussion of courtly affairs and noble dynasties soon gives way to cultured entertainment.
Expensive wine flows like water. You, too, ask a couple noble ladies to dance and show your skill.
You return to your hotel room in the small hours of the night, with just enough strength left to undress before your aching head and feet make you collapse.
For the first time in your life, you have mingled with a noble crowd on your own, without your family’s aid.

When the clock tower strikes eight, your new acquaintances proceed to a rich house not too far away..
Candlelight fills the halls before you, reflected in abundant mirrors and gilded picture frames. Manservants bring drinks and refreshments to every guest.

There are the sounds of music, and laughter, and small talk.
Here and there you see couples dancing to the music.
It appears you have made it to a small noble party.

The nobles are gathered in groups. You take the time to get introduced to each of them and join in their small talk.
Some discuss their studies at the College, while others relay fresh gossip. Have you heard that a Milanidas carriage was seen in the city the other day?
You mention how you once encountered Octavia Milanidas, daughter and heiress to the Archduke of Magra, at a square in Anizotte. These words draw a small crowd.

The Milanidas dynasty rarely, if ever, visits Eterna. They say it is the only house that can stand its ground against the Imperial Tempest dynasty. 
One young man even allows himself a little joke: they say the great Arknian houses turn to a Milanidas only when a Tempest needs to be refused — after all, only the Milanidas dynasty still knows how to say “no.”

But there is more. It turns out all humans owe the Milanidas dynasty for their foray into nobility: Char Milanidas was the Arknian who opened the first College, and its graduates were the first to be ennobled by the Mantle!
To feed and nourish their barren land, the dukes of Magra took to industry and began adopting innovative industrial and social practices. The dynasty’s motto is “Remembrance and Majesty” — but “Strife and Change” would suit them better.

Then the nobles start discussing the other great Arknian dynasties.
The Tempest dynasty is the first of the first, naturally — marked by the Twins, anointed to rule. All Tempests are known for their sincerity often bordering on a volatile temper, yet it is this very passion that has led them throughout history.
The Tempests have been chosen by the gods to rule the Empire.

The Diamant dynasty are the main supporters of the Emperor’s family, honor personified. The Diamants preside at the Arknian Courts of Honor that remain throughout the Empire in spite of the public taboo. These courts hold more sway over the laws and lives of the nobility than Imperial edits or prefectural authorities. 
Some mention Patriarch Junius Diamant, the black sheep of his own dynasty. He preaches the New Faith that rejects the Lots and stirs the minds of the common folk.

The Orgrif dynasty is another noble bloodline favored by the Emperor. They zealously advocate the Twins’ Faith and see the Empire as the union between heaven and earth. Every year the Orgrifs donate enough funds to build new temples across the Empire.

You enter the establishment and find a free seat next to a group of well-dressed young men and women.
Soon the hall fills with people, packed wall to wall. A richly dressed elderly man with a tenacious gaze and a wrinkled forehead appears before the audience.

You make your way back to your hotel room. You are absolutely shocked.
There are so many people in the capital who openly defy the Lots! How different they are from the listless, lethargic people of Anizotte!
You think of Gloria before you drift off to sleep. She would have been overjoyed to be present at a gathering like this…

“My name is Gert Arkwright, and I’m an industrialist from Eliria. I should start off with a few short words about myself. Just like you, I was born in the common estate. My father was a hardworking miner. The mine broke his back, and he died of natural causes. My mother used to say that was his Lot: you work, you endure, and you suffer.
“Well, now I’m the owner of five ore processing factories, and every day gets me thinking. How come a son of a run-of-the-mill miner and a wealthy industrialist have to live by the same Lot?

“Tell me this, now: is it just and fair that a man who owns a factory has the same meager rights as an ordinary farmer? If you own several stores and command the workers almost like a noble commands an army, must you really suffer like a lowborn man? Even if you can afford good clothing, good food, and a good house like a nobleman, even if you live and stand closer to the nobles than farmers and tinkers and manservants?”

His introduction sparks a debate. 
Most of the people in the hall side with Arkwright. They say that well-to-do people need not live by the commoners’ Lot.
There are outcries defending the holy function of the Lots, but they are quickly snuffed without support.

For the first time in your life, you see people daring to defy their Lot in public!
Emotions soon begin to run high. More and more people shout words of opposition to the current order of the Empire. They argue that industrialists, merchants, and other well-off people are no worse than the nobles and ought to have their say and their own rights!
